Source energy is separate sum over outgoing wave directions, not coherent junction energy.

limitations: The recording benefits are small and do not establish audibility, market rank or perceptual equivalence.

Dry and Walden training total scores are slightly worse while attacks improve; the predeclared total degradation ceiling was0.5%. All exact term scores and denominators available in the input reports are retained.

The flat-top and GuitarSet results are monitors. GuitarSet log-magnitude MAE and chroma distance worsen slightly while spectral convergence improves; no monitor result was used to fit contact gains or delay paths.
The fixed noise-derived contact burst is phenomenological displacement-wave excitation, not a measured force/contact law.
Native source-energy conservation refers to the separate outgoing wave directions, not coherent junction energy, microphone RMS or a complete external work budget.
First-arrival dispersion and ordinary string-frequency loss are omitted; release/touch hand damping is applied on arrival.
Travel delays freeze at contact. Rapid fret/bend/MPE changes during the burst are finite but are not physically retimed.
The existing retained-tail policy keeps only the immediately preceding vertical branch; this change does not create unlimited retrigger history or reciprocal horizontal bridge coupling.
Held-note invariance excludes release/refret/retrigger/pedal transitions, which have separate native tests. Six GuitarSet performance renders also remain byte-identical across lifecycle changes.
Real-recording references have uncertain or unmatched instruments, captures and gestures as detailed in each source protocol. Descriptor scores are not controlled physical parameter identifications.
Final callback timing and its corrected named-model metadata are intentionally absent; root will attach their raw-data/provenance hashes separately.
Callback diagnostic excludes JUCE and host overhead; occasional deadline misses on baseline and candidate preclude a hard realtime safety claim.
